newsitem.title: KENYA: Lufthansa sees '97 Kenya cargo at 15,000mt.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa sees '97 Kenya cargo at 15,000mt.

text.p: German freight carrier Lufthansa Cargo expects to transport a total of 15,000 tonnes of air cargo on its route from the Kenyan capital of Nairobi to Frankfurt in 1997, a senior manager said.
This is a 25 percent increase compared to the 12,000 tonnes of cargo the carrier transported in 1996, David Keary, general manager for Lufthansa Cargo in East and Central Africa said.
"This year we hope to do about 15,000 tonnes of cargo for all of the year. We had about 12,000 tonnes of cargo in 1996 so we are talking about a 25 percent increase," Keary told Reuters.

"Business has been very, very good for us, we have had very successful growth rates in the past few years. Our turnover in Nairobi is even bigger than Johannesburg, with about 30 percent more in total tonnage," he said.

Lufthansa Cargo currently flies three weekly Boeing-747 freighters between Nairobi and Frankfurt with a capacity of just over 100 tonnes of cargo each. In addition an average of 20 tonnes a week is shipped on Lufthansa's three weekly passenger flights, all Airbus 310s.

Keary said Lufthansa Cargo in the past two years had seen a 63 percent increase in the volume of exports from Kenya, mostly in cut flowers, vegetables and fresh fish fillets from Lake Victoria, which borders Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

The horticulture industry and fresh fish were making up the biggest share of cargo on the Nairobi route, with cut flowers and fresh fish accounting for about 30 percent each of total volume, while vegetables makes up about 25 percent, he said.
The remaining 15 percent of cargo consisted mostly of personal belongings, machine parts and electrical goods, said Keary, adding that Lufthansa's freight flights were "more or less full both ways".
While Lufthansa's growth had been high, Keary estimated the average growth rate in the air cargo industry in Kenya to have been around 5.0 percent over the past three years.
But he said growth in especially the horticulture industry remained high and from next October Lufthansa Cargo planned to increase its route frequency from three to four weekly freight flights.
"We are now concentrating on all fresh products; flowers, vegetables and fresh fish and we'll plan to increase to four frequencies a week from October," Keary said in an interview.
Kenya produced some 90,000 tonnes of fresh produce in 1996, of which cut flowers to the European flower auctions in Holland and Germany accounted for about 45,000 tonnes.
Some 90 percent of all fresh produce is shipped by air freight.

"We have specialised in a lot of fresh products here with our fresh-to-door service where we sent all parisable products to Frankfurt, wherefrom it's send to a huge specialised perishable handling center, wherefrom the goods are distributed through thermo, refrigerated, trucks to its final destinations.

"This is a unique service because it makes sure the products are delivered on time without any interfering in the cool chain which of course ensures the highest possible quality of fresh products," said Keary.

He said the fresh-to-door service, which was introduced by Lufthansa Cargo globally a few years ago, in East Africa has led to 98 percent of all the carrier's cargo go to German destinations, up from 60 percent of total cargo before.
